column2: Astronomers report a series of incandescent flashes on the planet Mars, close to its opposition. Some speak of a huge outbreak of burning gas on the planet. The newspapers treat it as a curiosity.

Mars is once again at opposition, and again the flashes have been seen. Last night a falling star was observed over the south of England, leaving a greenish streak behind it. It seems to have come down somewhere near Oxford.
Send someone to look at it.

The 'meteorite' is no meteorite. It is a huge cylinder, half buried in a sandpit, and its lid is slowly unscrewing from the inside. Crowds have gathered at the edge of the pit. Something is alive in there.
Send in the army before it opens!
Send a deputation under a white flag.
The cylinder has come to rest on the third planet. While the lid unscrews, the crew prepares to emerge. The natives are gathering at the edge of the pit.
With a clang, the lid of the cylinder has fallen into the pit. Where the pit is still ours, the crew emerges and begins assembling the fighting machines.
The humans reached the pit before the machines were ready. Artillery has torn the cylinder apart, and its crew perished inside.
A small party of humans approached the pit under a white flag. The Heat-Ray burned them where they stood. The conquest begins.
Assembly is complete. A score of towering three-legged machines rise out of the pit, each armed with the Heat-Ray.
The humans of $PROVINCENAME$ have been rounded up and penned. They will labour, and they will feed the Martians.
With the Martians driven out of $PROVINCENAME$, the survivors of the pens stumble out into the light, broken and angry.
The fighting machines have held $PROVINCENAME$ for months. The Martians now treat it as their own.
Mars is at opposition once more. A new volley of cylinders has been launched towards the third planet.
Another cylinder from Mars has come down in our land. The Martians claim the ground around their pit.
Our provinces have been out of Martian hands for months. The Martian claim to them is broken, and they are ours again.
Not all of the humans on our borders are at war with us yet.
Fighting machines have crossed into our territory. There will be no negotiation.
A blood-red weed has sprung up around the Martian works in $PROVINCENAME$, choking the fields.
The red weed has crept into $PROVINCENAME$ from the Martian lands, clogging rivers and smothering crops.
The pens have been culled again. Fed on human blood, the crews keep the machines walking.
Another cylinder has come down on the third planet. The crew will soon begin to unscrew the lid.
Another of the cylinders has come down in England, not far from the first.
The fighting machines stride on towards any human nation not yet at war with us.
Some of our provinces have slipped out of our grasp. Those not retaken in time will return to the humans.
Not all of the humans around us are at war with us yet.
The crews in every pit we hold have begun assembling a new batch of fighting machines. In twenty days they will be ready, if the pits are still ours.
The cylinder was not empty. Before the lid has even fallen, the first fighting machines have been assembled and stride out of the pit.
A new batch of fighting machines has risen from our pits.
Our scouts report a great clamour of machinery from the Martian pit near our border. New fighting machines will rise within weeks unless the pit is taken first.
The Martians have dug a great pit at $PROVINCENAME$. From here, too, fighting machines will soon rise.
